主要内容: The U.S. manufacturing sector expanded in April 2015 for the 28th consecutive month, with the PMI® at 51.5%, the same as March. New Orders increased to 53.5%, up 1.7 percentage points from March. Production rose to 56%, a 2.2 percentage point increase. Employment contracted to 48.3%, down 1.7 percentage points from March. Inventories of raw materials fell to 49.5%, a 2 percentage point decrease. Prices decreased to 40.5%, up 1.5 percentage points from March. While the PMI® remained unchanged, 15 of the 18 manufacturing industries reported growth in April, indicating a broader distribution of growth. The two industries reporting contraction were Apparel, Leather & Allied Products, and Computer & Electronic Products. Respondents noted low energy costs, strong automotive demand, and challenges with labor availability. The April 2015 Manufacturing PMI® registered at 51.5 percent, indicating continued expansion in the manufacturing sector for the 28th consecutive month. A PMI® above 50 percent signifies growth, and the 51.5 reading corresponds to a 2.6 percent annualized increase in real GDP. The New Orders Index rose to 53.5 percent, marking the 29th consecutive month of growth in new orders. The Production Index increased to 56 percent, reflecting the 32nd consecutive month of production growth. However, the Employment Index declined to 48.3 percent, indicating contraction in employment for the first time in over a year. The report also highlighted that commodities such as aluminum, crude oil, and steel saw price declines, while freight prices rose. The data suggests a mixed performance in the manufacturing sector, with growth in production and orders but a contraction in employment.
